current_description.description_long: An Associated Press report from October 11, 2023, describes testimony by a retired bank official at the New York civil-fraud trial brought by Attorney General Letitia James against Donald Trump, his company, and top executives. The official testified that Trump’s financial statements were key to the bank’s approval of a $125 million loan in 2011 for Trump’s Doral golf resort in Florida and a $107 million loan in 2012 for his Chicago hotel and tower. AP reported that this was the first time a bank official testified in court about the statements’ effect on Trump’s ability to obtain loans. The trial concerned whether financial statements used for lending were fraudulent, but this testimony does not establish that expenses were billed twice through internal loans. The supplied article and prior notes do not identify a duplicated expense, an internal-loan transaction, or a judicial finding on that alleged mechanism. The title is narrowed to the specific lending testimony the cited report supports.

frozen_original.title: Trump Organization Double-Billed Expenses Through Internal Loans — NY Fraud Trial Finding
frozen_original.synopsis: During New York's civil fraud trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Trump Organization executives engaged in a scheme of double-billing expenses by routing them through internal intercompany loans that were never repaid. The practice artificially inflated the profitability of certain properties while hiding expenses that would reduce asset valuations. The double-billing scheme was systematic enough that Judge Arthur Engoron found it to be a deliberate pattern rather than accounting error. The findings revealed a corporate culture of deliberate financial manipulation stretching back years across multiple Trump business units. Several Trump Organization executives had previously pleaded guilty to related charges.

proposal.exact_defects: The timing and sequence are wrong. Reuters reports broad HHS layoffs beginning April 1, 2025, while later reporting shows Jeanne Marrazzo was placed on administrative leave and ultimately dismissed after later whistleblower activity. I did not find evidence that RFK Jr. fired Marrazzo and dozens of senior NIH scientists in March 2025 as one action.

proposal.original_claim_summary: RFK Jr. Fires NIH Scientists Including Fauci Deputy Jeanne Marrazzo
proposal.original_synopsis: In March 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. ordered the firing of dozens of senior NIH scientists, including Dr. Jeanne Marrazzo — the director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) who had replaced Dr. Anthony Fauci — along with other prominent researchers overseeing HIV/AIDS, vaccine development, and infectious disease research. The firings were carried out without cause or transition planning, disrupting ongoing clinical trials and long-term research programs. Scientists described receiving abrupt termination notices while mid-experiment. International collaborators warned U.S. scientific credibility and partnerships were at risk. The move was part of a broader ideological purge of career scientists deemed insufficiently loyal to Kennedy's anti-establishment health agenda.

proposal.original_claim_summary: DHS revokes visas based on social media posts critical of Israel
proposal.original_synopsis: The Department of Homeland Security began revoking visas of individuals who had made social media posts critical of Israel, using immigration enforcement as a tool to punish protected political speech. Students, academics, and professionals had their visas cancelled after DHS officials identified social media content expressing opposition to Israeli government policies. The action represented a chilling conflation of immigration enforcement with political censorship.
